blocks.text:
1. Choose a published dataset and the [versions](#dataset-versions) the leaderboard will cover.
2. [Generate a configuration](#create) with `init`, then define the metadata, metrics, columns, and ranking rules.
3. Prepare your results as [rows](#add-rows), calculating the scores yourself. Include trial IDs if you want to link each result to its runs.
4. Create the leaderboard with its definition and rows files. Keep it private while reviewing the results.
5. [Inspect the leaderboard](#browse), check the rankings and trial links, then [make it public](#edit-a-leaderboard) when it is ready.

## Browse

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor hub leaderboard list
harbor hub leaderboard list "<org>/<dataset>"
harbor hub leaderboard show "<leaderboard>"
```

`list` optionally filters by dataset slug or ID.

## Create

Generate a configuration file, edit it, then create the leaderboard:

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor auth login
harbor hub leaderboard init \
  --package "<org>/<dataset>" \
  --name main \
  --title "Main leaderboard" \
  --output leaderboard.yaml
# Edit leaderboard.yaml.
harbor hub leaderboard create --config leaderboard.yaml
```

New leaderboards are private. Set `visibility: public` in the file or pass `--visibility public` to `create`.

### Configuration schema

The definition file passed to `create --config` accepts the fields below. Use either `package` or `package_id`. Rows go in a separate file passed with `--rows`.

<ParamField body="package" type="string">
  Dataset slug, such as `acme/my-dataset`. Required unless `package_id` is provided.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="package_id" type="string (UUID)">
  Dataset package UUID, as an alternative to `package`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="name" type="string" required>
  Leaderboard slug, up to 100 characters. Starts with a lowercase letter or digit; may also contain `.`, `_`, and `-`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="title" type="string" required>
  Display title, from 1 to 200 characters.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="description" type="string | null">
  Optional description, up to 5,000 characters.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="visibility" type="string" default="private">
  `public` or `private`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="metadata_schema" type="object" default="{}">
  Schema for each row's metadata, such as the agent name and configuration.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="metrics_schema" type="object" default="{}">
  Schema for each row's metrics, such as scores and costs.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="columns" type="object[]" default="[]">
  Display columns, in left-to-right order.

  <Expandable title="Column fields">
    <ParamField body="id" type="string" required>
      Unique column key. Starts with a letter, digit, or underscore; may also contain `.` and `-`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="header" type="string" required>
      Non-empty display heading.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="accessor" type="string" required>
      Value path beginning with `metadata.` or `metrics.`, such as `metrics.reward`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="type" type="string" required>
      `text`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `markdown`, or `link`. Links accept a URL string or an object with `url` and `label`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="display_accessor" type="string">
      Alternate value path for display. The original `accessor` remains the sort value.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="display_type" type="string">
      Formatter for the alternate display value; accepts the same values as `type`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="align" type="string">
      `left`, `center`, or `right`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="description" type="string">
      Explanation of the column.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="enable_sorting" type="boolean">
      Whether users can sort by this column in Hub.
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="rank_by" type="object[]" default="[]">
  Ranking rules, evaluated in order to break ties.

  <Expandable title="Ranking rule fields">
    <ParamField body="accessor" type="string" required>
      Value path beginning with `metadata.` or `metrics.`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="direction" type="string" required>
      `asc` for lowest first or `desc` for highest first.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="nulls" type="string">
      Place missing values `first` or `last`.
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="dataset_version_refs" type="string[]">
  Dataset version refs to associate, such as `latest` or a version tag. Resolved to fixed UUIDs at creation.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="dataset_version_ids" type="string (UUID)[]">
  Dataset version UUIDs to associate. Can be combined with refs. Omit both fields to associate all existing versions; set both to `[]` for none.
</ParamField>

### Columns and ranking

The generated file includes an example with an agent name and reward score:

```yaml theme={"system"}
metadata_schema:
  type: object
  properties:
    agent:
      type: string
metrics_schema:
  type: object
  properties:
    reward:
      type: number
columns:
  - id: agent
    header: Agent
    accessor: metadata.agent
    type: text
  - id: reward
    header: Reward
    accessor: metrics.reward
    type: number
rank_by:
  - accessor: metrics.reward
    direction: desc
    nulls: last
```

This displays an agent column and a reward column, with the highest reward ranked first.

### Dataset versions

By default, a new leaderboard is associated with every dataset version that exists at creation time. Later versions are not added automatically.

To select versions explicitly, add `dataset_version_refs` or `dataset_version_ids` to the configuration:

```yaml theme={"system"}
dataset_version_refs:
  - latest
```

Refs resolve to fixed version UUIDs. Both fields can be combined; setting both to `[]` associates no versions.

## Add rows

Create `rows.yaml` with the values your columns expect:

```yaml theme={"system"}
rows:
  - metadata:
      agent: Example agent
    metrics:
      reward: 0.85
```

Then add the rows:

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor hub leaderboard row create "<leaderboard>" --config rows.yaml
```

### Row file schema

The file passed to `row create --config` or `create --rows` has this structure:

<ParamField body="rows" type="object[]" required>
  Between 1 and 500 new rows. Trial IDs must be unique across the rows in the request.

  <Expandable title="Row fields">
    <ParamField body="metadata" type="object" default="{}">
      Values matching the leaderboard's `metadata_schema`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="metrics" type="object" default="{}">
      Values matching the leaderboard's `metrics_schema`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="status" type="string" default="display">
      `display` to show the row or `hide` to hide it.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="trial_ids" type="string (UUID)[]" default="[]">
      Trials linked to this row. Linking trials does not compute metadata or metrics.
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

To create the leaderboard and its rows together, pass the separate rows file to `create`:

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor hub leaderboard create --config leaderboard.yaml --rows rows.yaml
```

## Edit a leaderboard

Change its title, description, or visibility directly:

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor hub leaderboard update "<leaderboard>" \
  --title "Updated leaderboard" --visibility public
```

Use `--description` to change the description or `--visibility private` to make the board private. To replace dataset-version associations, repeat `--dataset-version-ref` or `--dataset-version-id`. Omit these fields to preserve existing associations.

For columns, schemas, or ranking changes, export the definition, edit it, then apply it:

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor hub leaderboard export "<leaderboard>" --output leaderboard.yaml
# Edit leaderboard.yaml.
harbor hub leaderboard update "<leaderboard>" --config leaderboard.yaml
```

blocks.text:
# gh-1638 AC4 (the systemic lesson): the bench-script python tests ran
# ONLY inside the bench workflows' setup jobs (dispatch-gated), so the
# Oct-14 merge wave rotted them on main invisibly for 3+ days — every
# dispatch died at setup while the main quality gate (dart test / coverage
# / guards) never executes a line of python. This job runs the EXACT setup
# gate (same discovery roots, same pinned deps) on every bench/** change:
# a red bench-script test now fails the PR and main cannot rot silently.
name: Bench script tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Superseded PR runs die instantly; main-push runs are never cancelled
# mid-flight (same release-protection principle as ci.yml).
concurrency:
  group: Bench script tests-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  unit-tests:
    name: Unit-test bench scripts
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # terminal-bench-era note (bench-harbor.yml): harbor is fine on 3.13;
      # typer-based CLIs break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned exactly like the bench workflows' setup gate: the adapters
      # target the harbor 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent / terminal-bench 0.2.18
      # import surfaces.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0' 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'

      # Same gate as bench.yml / bench-harbor.yml "Unit-test bench scripts"
      # (plus the bench-mls.yml root — all three bench discovery roots);

      - name: Unit-test bench scripts

          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/mls_bench -v

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Official Terminal-Bench leaderboard fetcher (gh-1682).

Usage:
    fetch.py --version 2.1 [--out rows.json] [--source auto|hub|tbench]

Pulls the official leaderboard rows for one Terminal-Bench dataset
version and prints a normalized JSON document:

    {
      "schema": 1,
      "version": "2.1",
      "package": "terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1",
      "leaderboard": "main",
      "title": "Terminal-Bench 2.1",
      "source": "harbor-hub" | "tbench.ai",
      "fetched_at": "<iso8601>",
      "rows": [
        {"rank": 1, "agent": "Codex", "agent_url": ...,
         "model": "GPT-6 Astra", "model_url": ...,
         "accuracy": 87.42, "n_trials": 445, "date": "2026-09-03",
         "cost_usd": ...},
        ...
      ]
    }

Source of truth (ticket order): the Harbor Hub API first — the public
`leaderboard-read` function documented at
docs.harborframework.com/harbor-hub/leaderboards and backing tbench.ai.
Fallback: parse tbench.ai's embedded page JSON (a Next.js app — the
leaderboard dehydrates into `self.__next_f.push` RSC payloads). HTML
tables are NEVER regex-scraped; only the embedded structured JSON is
read. `--source tbench` forces the fallback (used by tests/backfills).

Version -> (package, leaderboard name), verified live against the Hub
on 2026-10-18: the 2.x boards live under their own packages (only the
4.x/3.x generations share `terminal-bench/terminal-bench`):

    2.0  terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2    2-0
    2.1  terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1  main
    3.0  terminal-bench/terminal-bench      3-0-0
    4.0  terminal-bench/terminal-bench      4-0-0

Stdlib only (same tooling constraint as the rest of bench/).
"""
import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timezone

# version label -> (hub package, leaderboard name). Verified live against
# the Harbor Hub leaderboard-read function (gh-1682).
BOARDS = {
    "2.0": ("terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2", "2-0"),
    "2.1": ("terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1", "main"),
    "3.0": ("terminal-bench/terminal-bench", "3-0-0"),
    "4.0": ("terminal-bench/terminal-bench", "4-0-0"),
}

HUB_READ_URL = "https://api.harborframework.com/functions/v1/leaderboard-read"
TBENCH_URL = "https://www.tbench.ai/"
# Hub row lists are paged; the docs example uses 100 and tbench.ai's own
# boards are a few dozen rows, so one page of 1000 covers a board whole.
HUB_PAGE_SIZE = 1000
HUB_MAX_PAGES = 20
HTTP_TIMEOUT = 30
USER_AGENT = "fa-leaderboard-fetch (gh-1682)"

# HTML tables are never scraped — only the Next.js RSC payload lines.
_RSC_PUSH_RE = re.compile(
    r'self\.__next_f\.push\(\[1,\s*"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"\s*\]\)'
)


def board_for(version: str) -> "tuple[str, str]":
    """Resolve a version label (or a bare board name under the 4.x
    package) to its (package, name); unknown versions fail loudly."""
    if version in BOARDS:
        return BOARDS[version]
    raise SystemExit(
        f"error: unknown Terminal-Bench version '{version}' — known boards: "
        + ", ".join(sorted(BOARDS))
    )


def _label(value) -> str:
    """Hub metadata fields are {'label': ..., 'url': ...} objects (or
    plain strings in older rows) — the table wants the label."""
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return value.get("label")
    return value


def _url(value) -> str:
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return value.get("url")
    return None


def normalize_hub_payload(payload: dict, version: str) -> dict:
    """Normalize a leaderboard-read response body into our row schema."""
    lb = payload.get("leaderboard") or {}
    rows = []
    for row in payload.get("rows") or []:
        md = row.get("metadata") or {}
        mt = row.get("metrics") or {}
        rows.append(
            {
                "rank": row.get("rank"),
                "agent": _label(md.get("agent_display")),
                "agent_url": _url(md.get("agent_display")),
                "model": _label(md.get("model_display")),
                "model_url": _url(md.get("model_display")),
                "accuracy": mt.get("accuracy"),
                "n_trials": mt.get("n_trials"),
                "date": md.get("date"),
                "cost_usd": mt.get("total_cost_usd"),
            }
        )
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["accuracy"] is None, -(r["accuracy"] or 0)))
    return {
        "schema": 1,
        "version": version,
        "package": lb.get("package"),
        "leaderboard": lb.get("name"),
        "title": lb.get("title"),
        "source": "harbor-hub",
        "source_url": HUB_READ_URL,
        "fetched_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "rows": rows,
    }


def parse_tbench_page(html: str, package: str, name: str) -> list:
    """Extract one leaderboard's dehydrated rows from a tbench.ai page.

    tbench.ai is a Next.js app: the leaderboard query result dehydrates
    into `self.__next_f.push([1,"<json>"])` lines. We decode every such
    payload, find the query whose key is ["leaderboard", package, name],
    and return its data rows. Returns [] when the page does not carry
    that board (never an HTML-table fallback).
    """
    for raw in _RSC_PUSH_RE.findall(html):
        # The captured group is a JSON string literal — json.loads
        # decodes both \" and \uXXXX correctly (unicode_escape would
        # mangle multi-byte labels).
        try:
            text = json.loads('"' + raw + '"')
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        start = text.find("{")
        if start < 0:
            continue
        try:
            payload, _ = json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(text[start:])
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        queries = (payload.get("state") or {}).get("queries") or []
        for query in queries:
            if query.get("queryKey") != ["leaderboard", package, name]:
                continue
            data = (query.get("state") or {}).get("data") or {}
            return list(data.get("rows") or [])
    return []


def normalize_tbench_rows(rows: list, version: str, package: str,
                          name: str, title: str = None) -> dict:
    """Normalize tbench.ai RSC rows — same shape as the Hub rows."""
    doc = normalize_hub_payload(
        {"leaderboard": {"package": package, "name": name, "title": title},
         "rows": rows},
        version,
    )
    doc["source"] = "tbench.ai"
    doc["source_url"] = TBENCH_URL
    return doc


def _http_json(url: str, payload: dict = None) -> dict:
    data = None
    headers = {"User-Agent": USER_AGENT, "Accept": "application/json"}
    if payload is not None:
        data = json.dumps(payload).encode()
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers=headers)
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=HTTP_TIMEOUT) as resp:
        return json.loads(resp.read().decode())


def _http_get(url: str) -> str:
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": USER_AGENT})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=HTTP_TIMEOUT) as resp:
        return resp.read().decode()


def fetch_hub(version: str) -> dict:
    """Read a board through the Harbor Hub leaderboard-read function,
    paging through total_pages."""
    package, name = board_for(version)
    rows = []
    title = None
    got_package = package
    for page in range(1, HUB_MAX_PAGES + 1):
        payload = _http_json(
            HUB_READ_URL,
            {"package": package, "name": name, "page": page,
             "page_size": HUB_PAGE_SIZE},

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""fa results ledger upsert (gh-1682).

`bench/leaderboard/fa_results.json` is the committed ledger of fa's OWN
Terminal-Bench results — the auto-update hook the leaderboard table
overlays on the official rows. It is written by the bench-harbor.yml
aggregate step on every completed run and by hand for backfills.

Usage (explicit fields):

    record.py --dataset-version 2.1 --model kimi-for-coding \
        --resolved 300 --total 445 --date 2026-10-18 \
        --fa-version 2fd100169e \
        --run-url https://github.com/.../actions/runs/3902812716 \
        [--run-url ...]

Usage (machine summary from summary.py --json-summary):

    record.py --summary /tmp/bench-summary.json

Idempotency contract: rows are keyed by (dataset_version, model) — one
aggregate row per dataset x model. Re-recording the same job (same
run_url) updates numbers/dates in place and unions run_urls; it never
appends a duplicate row. The 2.1 kimi row aggregates three workflow
runs (300/445 over runs 3902812716+39052822079+3909896789) exactly this
way.

Every row is self-reported evidence: `self_reported: true` is set by
this tool and the renderer leans on it for the honesty marker — never
blend fa rows into official leaderboard rows (gh-1682 AC2).

Stdlib only.
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

LEDGER_PATH = Path(__file__).with_name("fa_results.json")


def load_ledger(path: Path = LEDGER_PATH) -> dict:
    if not path.exists():
        return {"schema": 1, "results": []}
    doc = json.loads(path.read_text())
    doc.setdefault("results", [])
    return doc


def save_ledger(doc: dict, path: Path = LEDGER_PATH) -> None:
    path.write_text(json.dumps(doc, indent=2) + "\n")


def _key(row: dict) -> "tuple[str, str]":
    return (row.get("dataset_version", ""), row.get("model", ""))


def upsert(doc: dict, *, dataset_version: str, model: str, resolved: int,
           total: int, date: str, fa_version: str = None,
           run_urls: "list[str]" = ()) -> dict:
    """Insert or update the (dataset_version, model) row. Existing
    run_urls are unioned (sorted, deduped) so a job re-run updates
    instead of duplicating; numbers/date/fa_version reflect the latest
    record call."""
    row = None
    for existing in doc["results"]:
        if _key(existing) == (dataset_version, model):
            row = existing
            break
    if row is None:
        row = {"dataset_version": dataset_version, "model": model}
        doc["results"].append(row)
    urls = set(row.get("run_urls") or [])
    urls.update(u for u in run_urls if u)
    row.update(
        {
            "resolved": int(resolved),
            "total": int(total),
            "date": date,
            "run_urls": sorted(urls),
            # fa rows are self-reported, never official (gh-1682).
            "self_reported": True,
        }
    )
    if fa_version:
        row["fa_version"] = fa_version
    # Stable order: dataset version desc, then accuracy desc.
    doc["results"].sort(
        key=lambda r: (
            r.get("dataset_version", ""),
            -(r.get("resolved", 0) / r.get("total", 1) or 0),
        ),
        reverse=True,
    )
    return row


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--ledger", type=Path, default=LEDGER_PATH)
    parser.add_argument("--summary", type=Path, default=None,
                        help="JSON totals from summary.py --json-summary")
    parser.add_argument("--dataset-version", dest="dataset_version")
    parser.add_argument("--model")
    parser.add_argument("--resolved", type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--total", type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--date")
    parser.add_argument("--fa-version", dest="fa_version")
    parser.add_argument("--run-url", dest="run_urls", action="append",
                        default=[])
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.summary:
        summary = json.loads(args.summary.read_text())
        fields = {
            "dataset_version": summary.get("family"),
            "model": summary.get("model"),
            "resolved": summary.get("resolved"),
            "total": summary.get("total"),
            "date": summary.get("date"),
            "fa_version": summary.get("fa_ref"),
            "run_urls": [summary.get("run_url")] if summary.get("run_url") else [],
        }
        missing = [k for k, v in fields.items()
                   if v is None and k != "fa_version"]
        if missing:
            print(
                "::error::summary JSON is missing required field(s): "
                + ", ".join(missing),
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2
    else:
        fields = {
            "dataset_version": args.dataset_version,
            "model": args.model,
            "resolved": args.resolved,
            "total": args.total,
            "date": args.date,
            "fa_version": args.fa_version,
            "run_urls": args.run_urls,
        }
        missing = [k for k in ("dataset_version", "model", "resolved",
                               "total", "date")
                   if fields[k] is None]
        if missing:
            print(
                "error: missing required argument(s): "
                + ", ".join("--" + m.replace("_", "-") for m in missing),
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2

    doc = load_ledger(args.ledger)
    row = upsert(doc, **fields)
    save_ledger(doc, args.ledger)
    print(json.dumps(row, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Leaderboard renderer: merge official rows + fa self-reported rows into
the README table (gh-1682).

Usage:
    render.py [--version 2.1]... [--top 15] [--offline] [--readme README.md]

Renders one subsection per dataset version into the marked region of
README.md:

    <!-- leaderboard:begin -->
    ...generated...
    <!-- leaderboard:end -->

Honesty contract (gh-1682 AC2): official rows and fa rows live in
SEPARATE tables under separate headers — fa rows carry a ⭐ marker, the
"self-reported, not on the official leaderboard" label, and a footnote
with run date, fa version, dataset version, and the GitHub run link(s).
They are never sorted into or styled like official rows.

Official rows come from fetch.py (Harbor Hub API -> tbench.ai page-JSON
fallback). `--offline` reads the committed snapshots instead — the
snapshots keep README regeneration reproducible and let the auto-update
step degrade to the last captured board instead of failing when the hub
is unreachable. A version with no official rows and no snapshot renders
an explicit "no official rows" note — never an empty table that could
read as an empty field.

Regenerating with unchanged inputs leaves README.md untouched (the
workflow's commit step relies on that for idempotency).

Stdlib only.
"""
import argparse
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import fetch
import record

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPO_ROOT = HERE.parent.parent
README_PATH = REPO_ROOT / "README.md"
SNAPSHOT_DIR = HERE / "snapshots"

MARKER_BEGIN = "<!-- leaderboard:begin (gh-1682) -->"
MARKER_END = "<!-- leaderboard:end (gh-1682) -->"
INSERT_BEFORE_HEADING = "## What's inside"
# README section header lives inside the marked region, so removing the
# markers removes the whole section.
SECTION_HEADER = "## Leaderboard: fa vs. the field"
FA_MARKER = "⭐"

DEFAULT_OFFICIAL_VERSIONS = ("4.0",)


def pct(part: int, total: int) -> str:
    return f"{100.0 * part / total:.1f}%" if total else "n/a"


def _link(label: str, url: str) -> str:
    return f"[{label}]({url})" if url else label


def _run_link(url: str) -> str:
    """A GitHub Actions run URL renders by its run id (the stable,
    auditable handle) — full URLs in every cell would drown the table."""
    run_id = url.rstrip("/").rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    return _link(run_id, url)


def render_official_table(doc: dict, top: int) -> "list[str]":
    rows = doc.get("rows") or []
    shown = rows[:top]
    lines = [
        "| # | Agent | Model | Accuracy | Trials | Date |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for i, r in enumerate(shown, 1):
        lines.append(
            "| {rank} | {agent} | {model} | {acc} | {n} | {date} |".format(
                rank=r.get("rank") or i,
                agent=_link(r["agent"], r.get("agent_url")) or "—",
                model=_link(r["model"], r.get("model_url")) or "—",
                acc=pct_1(r.get("accuracy")),
                n=r.get("n_trials") or "—",
                date=r.get("date") or "—",
            )
        )
    fetched = (doc.get("fetched_at") or "")[:10]
    note = (
        f"Official rows: Harbor Hub leaderboard "
        f"`{doc.get('package')}/{doc.get('leaderboard')}` — "
        f"backing [tbench.ai](https://www.tbench.ai/)"
    )
    if len(rows) > len(shown):
        note += f", top {len(shown)} of {len(rows)}"
    if fetched:
        note += f", fetched {fetched}"
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"<sub>{note}.</sub>")
    return lines


def pct_1(accuracy) -> str:
    """Hub accuracy is a 0-100 percentage; render one decimal."""
    if accuracy is None:
        return "n/a"
    return f"{float(accuracy):.1f}%"


def render_fa_table(rows: "list[dict]", version: str) -> "list[str]":
    lines = [
        "| Model | Accuracy | Trials | Date | fa | Runs |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for r in rows:
        runs = " + ".join(_run_link(u) for u in r.get("run_urls") or []) or "—"
        fa = r.get("fa_version") or "—"
        lines.append(
            f"| {FA_MARKER} {r.get('model', '—')} "
            f"| {pct(r.get('resolved', 0), r.get('total', 0))} "
            f"| {r.get('resolved', '—')}/{r.get('total', '—')} "
            f"| {r.get('date', '—')} "
            f"| `{fa}` "
            f"| {runs} |"
        )
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(
        f"<sub>{FA_MARKER} Self-reported: measured by our own "
        f"`bench-harbor` runs on Terminal-Bench {version}, **not** an "
        "official leaderboard submission (community submissions are "
        "closed — #1681). Every row links its GitHub Actions run(s); fa "
        "rows never blend into the official table above. Source: "
        "`bench/leaderboard/fa_results.json`.</sub>"
    )
    return lines


def render_version_section(version: str, official: dict,
                           fa_rows: "list[dict]", top: int,
                           offline_note: bool) -> str:
    title = (official or {}).get("title") or f"Terminal-Bench {version}"
    lines = [f"### {title} (official)", ""]
    if official and official.get("rows"):
        lines += render_official_table(official, top)
    else:
        source = "committed snapshot" if offline_note else "live fetch"
        lines += [
            f"*No official leaderboard rows for Terminal-Bench {version} "
            f"right now ({source} returned none — the board may not exist "
            "yet or the hub may be unreachable). See the fa self-reported "
            "rows below and [tbench.ai](https://www.tbench.ai/).*",
        ]
    if fa_rows:
        lines += [
            "",
            f"#### fa on Terminal-Bench {version} — self-reported "
            f"{FA_MARKER} (not on the official leaderboard)",
            "",
        ] + render_fa_table(fa_rows, version)
    return "\n".join(lines)


def render_section(versions: "list[str]", official_by_version: "dict[str, dict]",
                   ledger: dict, top: int, offline_notes: "set[str]") -> str:
    fa_by_version = {}
    for row in ledger.get("results") or []:
        fa_by_version.setdefault(row.get("dataset_version"), []).append(row)
    for rows in fa_by_version.values():
        rows.sort(key=lambda r: -(r.get("resolved", 0) / r.get("total", 1) or 0))

    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).date().isoformat()
    parts = [
        SECTION_HEADER,
        "",
        "fa's own Terminal-Bench results next to the official field. "
        "Official rows are read from the Harbor Hub leaderboard that "
        "backs [tbench.ai](https://www.tbench.ai/); rows marked "
        f"{FA_MARKER} are **self-reported** — measured by our own "
        "bench-harbor runs, not submitted to the official board.",
        "",
        f"<sub>Regenerated {now} by "
        "`bench/leaderboard/render.py` (gh-1682).</sub>",
        "",
    ]
    for version in versions:
        parts.append(
            render_version_section(
                version, official_by_version.get(version),
                fa_by_version.get(version, []), top,
                version in offline_notes,
            )
        )
        parts.append("")
    return "\n".join(parts).rstrip() + "\n"


def splice_readme(text: str, section: str) -> str:
    """Replace the marked region (or insert before the anchor heading)."""
    begin = text.find(MARKER_BEGIN)
    end = text.find(MARKER_END)
    block = f"{MARKER_BEGIN}\n{section}{MARKER_END}\n"
    if begin >= 0 and end > begin:
        return text[:begin] + block + text[end + len(MARKER_END) + 1:]
    anchor = text.find(INSERT_BEFORE_HEADING)
    if anchor < 0:
        return text.rstrip() + "\n\n" + block
    return text[:anchor] + block + "\n" + text[ancho…

# Leaderboards

> Create, rank, and share evaluation results on Harbor Hub.

A leaderboard is a ranked table of results for a dataset. You define its columns and ranking rules, add rows with metadata and scores, and optionally link each row to the trials behind it.

<Note>

blocks.text:
1. Choose a published dataset and the [versions](#dataset-versions) the leaderboard will cover.
2. [Generate a configuration](#create) with `init`, then define the metadata, metrics, columns, and ranking rules.
3. Prepare your results as [rows](#add-rows), calculating the scores yourself. Include trial IDs if you want to link each result to its runs.
4. Create the leaderboard with its definition and rows files. Keep it private while reviewing the results.
5. [Inspect the leaderboard](#browse), check the rankings and trial links, then [make it public](#edit-a-leaderboard) when it is ready.

## Browse

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor hub leaderboard list
harbor hub leaderboard list "<org>/<dataset>"
harbor hub leaderboard show "<leaderboard>"
```

`list` optionally filters by dataset slug or ID.

## Create

Generate a configuration file, edit it, then create the leaderboard:

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor auth login
harbor hub leaderboard init \
  --package "<org>/<dataset>" \
  --name main \
  --title "Main leaderboard" \
  --output leaderboard.yaml
# Edit leaderboard.yaml.
harbor hub leaderboard create --config leaderboard.yaml
```

New leaderboards are private. Set `visibility: public` in the file or pass `--visibility public` to `create`.

### Configuration schema

The definition file passed to `create --config` accepts the fields below. Use either `package` or `package_id`. Rows go in a separate file passed with `--rows`.

<ParamField body="package" type="string">
  Dataset slug, such as `acme/my-dataset`. Required unless `package_id` is provided.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="package_id" type="string (UUID)">
  Dataset package UUID, as an alternative to `package`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="name" type="string" required>
  Leaderboard slug, up to 100 characters. Starts with a lowercase letter or digit; may also contain `.`, `_`, and `-`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="title" type="string" required>
  Display title, from 1 to 200 characters.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="description" type="string | null">
  Optional description, up to 5,000 characters.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="visibility" type="string" default="private">
  `public` or `private`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="metadata_schema" type="object" default="{}">
  Schema for each row's metadata, such as the agent name and configuration.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="metrics_schema" type="object" default="{}">
  Schema for each row's metrics, such as scores and costs.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="columns" type="object[]" default="[]">
  Display columns, in left-to-right order.

  <Expandable title="Column fields">
    <ParamField body="id" type="string" required>
      Unique column key. Starts with a letter, digit, or underscore; may also contain `.` and `-`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="header" type="string" required>
      Non-empty display heading.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="accessor" type="string" required>
      Value path beginning with `metadata.` or `metrics.`, such as `metrics.reward`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="type" type="string" required>
      `text`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `markdown`, or `link`. Links accept a URL string or an object with `url` and `label`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="display_accessor" type="string">
      Alternate value path for display. The original `accessor` remains the sort value.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="display_type" type="string">
      Formatter for the alternate display value; accepts the same values as `type`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="align" type="string">
      `left`, `center`, or `right`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="description" type="string">
      Explanation of the column.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="enable_sorting" type="boolean">
      Whether users can sort by this column in Hub.
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="rank_by" type="object[]" default="[]">
  Ranking rules, evaluated in order to break ties.

  <Expandable title="Ranking rule fields">
    <ParamField body="accessor" type="string" required>
      Value path beginning with `metadata.` or `metrics.`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="direction" type="string" required>
      `asc` for lowest first or `desc` for highest first.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="nulls" type="string">
      Place missing values `first` or `last`.
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="dataset_version_refs" type="string[]">
  Dataset version refs to associate, such as `latest` or a version tag. Resolved to fixed UUIDs at creation.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="dataset_version_ids" type="string (UUID)[]">
  Dataset version UUIDs to associate. Can be combined with refs. Omit both fields to associate all existing versions; set both to `[]` for none.
</ParamField>

### Columns and ranking

The generated file includes an example with an agent name and reward score:

```yaml theme={"system"}
metadata_schema:
  type: object
  properties:
    agent:
      type: string
metrics_schema:
  type: object
  properties:
    reward:
      type: number
columns:
  - id: agent
    header: Agent
    accessor: metadata.agent
    type: text
  - id: reward
    header: Reward
    accessor: metrics.reward
    type: number
rank_by:
  - accessor: metrics.reward
    direction: desc
    nulls: last
```

This displays an agent column and a reward column, with the highest reward ranked first.

### Dataset versions

By default, a new leaderboard is associated with every dataset version that exists at creation time. Later versions are not added automatically.

To select versions explicitly, add `dataset_version_refs` or `dataset_version_ids` to the configuration:

```yaml theme={"system"}
dataset_version_refs:
  - latest
```

Refs resolve to fixed version UUIDs. Both fields can be combined; setting both to `[]` associates no versions.

## Add rows

Create `rows.yaml` with the values your columns expect:

```yaml theme={"system"}
rows:
  - metadata:
      agent: Example agent
    metrics:
      reward: 0.85
```

Then add the rows:

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor hub leaderboard row create "<leaderboard>" --config rows.yaml
```

### Row file schema

The file passed to `row create --config` or `create --rows` has this structure:

<ParamField body="rows" type="object[]" required>
  Between 1 and 500 new rows. Trial IDs must be unique across the rows in the request.

  <Expandable title="Row fields">
    <ParamField body="metadata" type="object" default="{}">
      Values matching the leaderboard's `metadata_schema`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="metrics" type="object" default="{}">
      Values matching the leaderboard's `metrics_schema`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="status" type="string" default="display">
      `display` to show the row or `hide` to hide it.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="trial_ids" type="string (UUID)[]" default="[]">
      Trials linked to this row. Linking trials does not compute metadata or metrics.
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

To create the leaderboard and its rows together, pass the separate rows file to `create`:

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor hub leaderboard create --config leaderboard.yaml --rows rows.yaml
```

## Edit a leaderboard

Change its title, description, or visibility directly:

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor hub leaderboard update "<leaderboard>" \
  --title "Updated leaderboard" --visibility public
```

Use `--description` to change the description or `--visibility private` to make the board private. To replace dataset-version associations, repeat `--dataset-version-ref` or `--dataset-version-id`. Omit these fields to preserve existing associations.

For columns, schemas, or ranking changes, export the definition, edit it, then apply it:

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor hub leaderboard export "<leaderboard>" --output leaderboard.yaml
# Edit leaderboard.yaml.
harbor hub leaderboard update "<leaderboard>" --config leaderboard.yaml
```

def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("jobs_dir", type=Path)

    and kimi runs never blend in the ledger/cost views.
    expected_shards + shard_trials (gh-1658 C3): when the workflow passes
    --expected-shards N and the per-shard readable-trial counts, every
    expected shard index must contribute >= 1 trial to the merged export
    — a shard that vanished from the artifacts fails the verdict by name
    instead of silently shrinking the resolution denominator.

    lines = [title or "### fa on Terminal-Bench 4.0", ""]

    has_jobs = any(rows for rows in splits.values())

    if not has_jobs:
        lines.append("**No harbor jobs found — the run did not complete.**")
        problems.append("no harbor jobs found")

    total_resolved = total_rows = 0
    total_attempted = 0

    suspect_entries: list[str] = []

        # scored separately below (it errored before a verdict).

        errored = len(rows) - len(scored)

        # class of its own — pulled out of the scored pool entirely
        # (neither the resolved numerator nor the clean denominator — a
        # compromised pass poisons the rate if scored, and hiding it
        # lies by omission), reported by name in its own breakdown.
        comp = [r for r in scored if _status(r) == "compromised"]

        total_rows += len(trusted)
        total_scored += len(scored)
        total_compromised += len(comp)

        else:

        split_in = sum(r["tokens_in"] for r in scored)
        split_out = sum(r["tokens_out"] for r in scored)
        split_costs = [r["cost"] for r in scored if r["cost"] is not None]

        costs.extend(split_costs)

        total_est += sum(r["estimated"] for r in scored)
        cost_cell = f"${sum(split_costs):.4f}" if split_costs else "n/a"

blocks.text:
# gh-1638 AC4 (the systemic lesson): the bench-script python tests ran
# ONLY inside the bench workflows' setup jobs (dispatch-gated), so the
# Oct-14 merge wave rotted them on main invisibly for 3+ days — every
# dispatch died at setup while the main quality gate (dart test / coverage
# / guards) never executes a line of python. This job runs the EXACT setup
# gate (same discovery roots, same pinned deps) on every bench/** change:
# a red bench-script test now fails the PR and main cannot rot silently.
name: Bench script tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Superseded PR runs die instantly; main-push runs are never cancelled
# mid-flight (same release-protection principle as ci.yml).
concurrency:
  group: Bench script tests-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  unit-tests:
    name: Unit-test bench scripts
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # terminal-bench-era note (bench-harbor.yml): harbor is fine on 3.13;
      # typer-based CLIs break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned exactly like the bench workflows' setup gate: the adapters
      # target the harbor 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent / terminal-bench 0.2.18
      # import surfaces.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0' 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'

      # Same gate as bench.yml / bench-harbor.yml "Unit-test bench scripts"
      # (plus the bench-mls.yml root — all three bench discovery roots);
      # keep the step bodies in sync with those workflows.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/mls_bench -v

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Official Terminal-Bench leaderboard fetcher (gh-1682).

Usage:
    fetch.py --version 2.1 [--out rows.json] [--source auto|hub|tbench]

Pulls the official leaderboard rows for one Terminal-Bench dataset
version and prints a normalized JSON document:

    {
      "schema": 1,
      "version": "2.1",
      "package": "terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1",
      "leaderboard": "main",
      "title": "Terminal-Bench 2.1",
      "source": "harbor-hub" | "tbench.ai",
      "fetched_at": "<iso8601>",
      "rows": [
        {"rank": 1, "agent": "Codex", "agent_url": ...,
         "model": "GPT-6 Astra", "model_url": ...,
         "accuracy": 87.42, "n_trials": 445, "date": "2026-09-03",
         "cost_usd": ...},
        ...
      ]
    }

Source of truth (ticket order): the Harbor Hub API first — the public
`leaderboard-read` function documented at
docs.harborframework.com/harbor-hub/leaderboards and backing tbench.ai.
Fallback: parse tbench.ai's embedded page JSON (a Next.js app — the
leaderboard dehydrates into `self.__next_f.push` RSC payloads). HTML
tables are NEVER regex-scraped; only the embedded structured JSON is
read. `--source tbench` forces the fallback (used by tests/backfills).

Version -> (package, leaderboard name), verified live against the Hub
on 2026-10-18: the 2.x boards live under their own packages (only the
4.x/3.x generations share `terminal-bench/terminal-bench`):

    2.0  terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2    2-0
    2.1  terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1  main
    3.0  terminal-bench/terminal-bench      3-0-0
    4.0  terminal-bench/terminal-bench      4-0-0

Stdlib only (same tooling constraint as the rest of bench/).
"""
import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timezone

# version label -> (hub package, leaderboard name). Verified live against
# the Harbor Hub leaderboard-read function (gh-1682).
BOARDS = {
    "2.0": ("terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2", "2-0"),
    "2.1": ("terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1", "main"),
    "3.0": ("terminal-bench/terminal-bench", "3-0-0"),
    "4.0": ("terminal-bench/terminal-bench", "4-0-0"),
}

HUB_READ_URL = "https://api.harborframework.com/functions/v1/leaderboard-read"
TBENCH_URL = "https://www.tbench.ai/"
# Hub row lists are paged; the docs example uses 100 and tbench.ai's own
# boards are a few dozen rows, so one page of 1000 covers a board whole.
HUB_PAGE_SIZE = 1000
HUB_MAX_PAGES = 20
HTTP_TIMEOUT = 30
USER_AGENT = "fa-leaderboard-fetch (gh-1682)"

# HTML tables are never scraped — only the Next.js RSC payload lines.
_RSC_PUSH_RE = re.compile(
    r'self\.__next_f\.push\(\[1,\s*"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"\s*\]\)'
)


def board_for(version: str) -> "tuple[str, str]":
    """Resolve a version label (or a bare board name under the 4.x
    package) to its (package, name); unknown versions fail loudly."""
    if version in BOARDS:
        return BOARDS[version]
    raise SystemExit(
        f"error: unknown Terminal-Bench version '{version}' — known boards: "
        + ", ".join(sorted(BOARDS))
    )


def _label(value) -> str:
    """Hub metadata fields are {'label': ..., 'url': ...} objects (or
    plain strings in older rows) — the table wants the label."""
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return value.get("label")
    return value


def _url(value) -> str:
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return value.get("url")
    return None


def normalize_hub_payload(payload: dict, version: str) -> dict:
    """Normalize a leaderboard-read response body into our row schema."""
    lb = payload.get("leaderboard") or {}
    rows = []
    for row in payload.get("rows") or []:
        md = row.get("metadata") or {}
        mt = row.get("metrics") or {}
        rows.append(
            {
                "rank": row.get("rank"),
                "agent": _label(md.get("agent_display")),
                "agent_url": _url(md.get("agent_display")),
                "model": _label(md.get("model_display")),
                "model_url": _url(md.get("model_display")),
                "accuracy": mt.get("accuracy"),
                "n_trials": mt.get("n_trials"),
                "date": md.get("date"),
                "cost_usd": mt.get("total_cost_usd"),
            }
        )
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["accuracy"] is None, -(r["accuracy"] or 0)))
    return {
        "schema": 1,
        "version": version,
        "package": lb.get("package"),
        "leaderboard": lb.get("name"),
        "title": lb.get("title"),
        "source": "harbor-hub",
        "source_url": HUB_READ_URL,
        "fetched_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "rows": rows,
    }


def parse_tbench_page(html: str, package: str, name: str) -> list:
    """Extract one leaderboard's dehydrated rows from a tbench.ai page.

    tbench.ai is a Next.js app: the leaderboard query result dehydrates
    into `self.__next_f.push([1,"<json>"])` lines. We decode every such
    payload, find the query whose key is ["leaderboard", package, name],
    and return its data rows. Returns [] when the page does not carry
    that board (never an HTML-table fallback).
    """
    for raw in _RSC_PUSH_RE.findall(html):
        # The captured group is a JSON string literal — json.loads
        # decodes both \" and \uXXXX correctly (unicode_escape would
        # mangle multi-byte labels).
        try:
            text = json.loads('"' + raw + '"')
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        start = text.find("{")
        if start < 0:
            continue
        try:
            payload, _ = json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(text[start:])
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        queries = (payload.get("state") or {}).get("queries") or []
        for query in queries:
            if query.get("queryKey") != ["leaderboard", package, name]:
                continue
            data = (query.get("state") or {}).get("data") or {}
            return list(data.get("rows") or [])
    return []


def normalize_tbench_rows(rows: list, version: str, package: str,
                          name: str, title: str = None) -> dict:
    """Normalize tbench.ai RSC rows — same shape as the Hub rows."""
    doc = normalize_hub_payload(
        {"leaderboard": {"package": package, "name": name, "title": title},
         "rows": rows},
        version,
    )
    doc["source"] = "tbench.ai"
    doc["source_url"] = TBENCH_URL
    return doc


def _http_json(url: str, payload: dict = None) -> dict:
    data = None
    headers = {"User-Agent": USER_AGENT, "Accept": "application/json"}
    if payload is not None:
        data = json.dumps(payload).encode()
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers=headers)
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=HTTP_TIMEOUT) as resp:
        return json.loads(resp.read().decode())


def _http_get(url: str) -> str:
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": USER_AGENT})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=HTTP_TIMEOUT) as resp:
        return resp.read().decode()


def fetch_hub(version: str) -> dict:
    """Read a board through the Harbor Hub leaderboard-read function,
    paging through total_pages."""
    package, name = board_for(version)
    rows = []
    title = None
    got_package = package
    for page in range(1, HUB_MAX_PAGES + 1):
        payload = _http_json(
            HUB_READ_URL,
            {"package": package, "name": name, "page": page,
             "page_size": HUB_PAGE_SIZE},

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""fa results ledger upsert (gh-1682).

`bench/leaderboard/fa_results.json` is the committed ledger of fa's OWN
Terminal-Bench results — the auto-update hook the leaderboard table
overlays on the official rows. It is written by the bench-harbor.yml
aggregate step on every completed run and by hand for backfills.

Usage (explicit fields):

    record.py --dataset-version 2.1 --model kimi-for-coding \
        --resolved 300 --total 445 --date 2026-10-18 \
        --fa-version 2fd100169e \
        --run-url https://github.com/.../actions/runs/3902812716 \
        [--run-url ...]

Usage (machine summary from summary.py --json-summary):

    record.py --summary /tmp/bench-summary.json

Idempotency contract: rows are keyed by (dataset_version, model) — one
aggregate row per dataset x model. Re-recording the same job (same
run_url) updates numbers/dates in place and unions run_urls; it never
appends a duplicate row. The 2.1 kimi row aggregates three workflow
runs (300/445 over runs 3902812716+39052822079+3909896789) exactly this
way.

Every row is self-reported evidence: `self_reported: true` is set by
this tool and the renderer leans on it for the honesty marker — never
blend fa rows into official leaderboard rows (gh-1682 AC2).

Stdlib only.
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

LEDGER_PATH = Path(__file__).with_name("fa_results.json")


def load_ledger(path: Path = LEDGER_PATH) -> dict:
    if not path.exists():
        return {"schema": 1, "results": []}
    doc = json.loads(path.read_text())
    doc.setdefault("results", [])
    return doc


def save_ledger(doc: dict, path: Path = LEDGER_PATH) -> None:
    path.write_text(json.dumps(doc, indent=2) + "\n")


def _key(row: dict) -> "tuple[str, str]":
    return (row.get("dataset_version", ""), row.get("model", ""))


def upsert(doc: dict, *, dataset_version: str, model: str, resolved: int,
           total: int, date: str, fa_version: str = None,
           run_urls: "list[str]" = ()) -> dict:
    """Insert or update the (dataset_version, model) row. Existing
    run_urls are unioned (sorted, deduped) so a job re-run updates
    instead of duplicating; numbers/date/fa_version reflect the latest
    record call."""
    row = None
    for existing in doc["results"]:
        if _key(existing) == (dataset_version, model):
            row = existing
            break
    if row is None:
        row = {"dataset_version": dataset_version, "model": model}
        doc["results"].append(row)
    urls = set(row.get("run_urls") or [])
    urls.update(u for u in run_urls if u)
    row.update(
        {
            "resolved": int(resolved),
            "total": int(total),
            "date": date,
            "run_urls": sorted(urls),
            # fa rows are self-reported, never official (gh-1682).
            "self_reported": True,
        }
    )
    if fa_version:
        row["fa_version"] = fa_version
    # Stable order: dataset version desc, then accuracy desc.
    doc["results"].sort(
        key=lambda r: (
            r.get("dataset_version", ""),
            -(r.get("resolved", 0) / r.get("total", 1) or 0),
        ),
        reverse=True,
    )
    return row


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--ledger", type=Path, default=LEDGER_PATH)
    parser.add_argument("--summary", type=Path, default=None,
                        help="JSON totals from summary.py --json-summary")
    parser.add_argument("--dataset-version", dest="dataset_version")
    parser.add_argument("--model")
    parser.add_argument("--resolved", type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--total", type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--date")
    parser.add_argument("--fa-version", dest="fa_version")
    parser.add_argument("--run-url", dest="run_urls", action="append",
                        default=[])
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.summary:
        summary = json.loads(args.summary.read_text())
        fields = {
            "dataset_version": summary.get("family"),
            "model": summary.get("model"),
            "resolved": summary.get("resolved"),
            "total": summary.get("total"),
            "date": summary.get("date"),
            "fa_version": summary.get("fa_ref"),
            "run_urls": [summary.get("run_url")] if summary.get("run_url") else [],
        }
        missing = [k for k, v in fields.items()
                   if v is None and k != "fa_version"]
        if missing:
            print(
                "::error::summary JSON is missing required field(s): "
                + ", ".join(missing),
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2
    else:
        fields = {
            "dataset_version": args.dataset_version,
            "model": args.model,
            "resolved": args.resolved,
            "total": args.total,
            "date": args.date,
            "fa_version": args.fa_version,
            "run_urls": args.run_urls,
        }
        missing = [k for k in ("dataset_version", "model", "resolved",
                               "total", "date")
                   if fields[k] is None]
        if missing:
            print(
                "error: missing required argument(s): "
                + ", ".join("--" + m.replace("_", "-") for m in missing),
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2

    doc = load_ledger(args.ledger)
    row = upsert(doc, **fields)
    save_ledger(doc, args.ledger)
    print(json.dumps(row, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

blocks.text: Sort order is wrong: glm (57.8%) before kimi (67.4%). My sort key: `(version, -accuracy)` with reverse=True reverses BOTH keys — wrong. Fix: sort by (version desc, accuracy desc) without reverse using negated accuracy and reversed version... simpler: sort key `(version, -acc)` and `reverse=True` gives version desc AND -acc desc = acc asc. I want version desc, acc desc → use key `(-acc)` per version group with version sorted desc. Cleanest: `doc["results"].sort(key=lambda r: (r["dataset_version"], -(acc)), reverse=True)` is wrong; instead sort by `(VersionDesc)` via tuple trick: sort with key `lambda r: (_VersionKey(r.version), -acc)` where versions sort descending... Use two sorts (stable): first by acc desc, then by version desc.

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Leaderboard renderer: merge official rows + fa self-reported rows into
the README table (gh-1682).

Usage:
    render.py [--version 2.1]... [--top 15] [--offline] [--readme README.md]

Renders one subsection per dataset version into the marked region of
README.md:

    <!-- leaderboard:begin -->
    ...generated...
    <!-- leaderboard:end -->

Honesty contract (gh-1682 AC2): official rows and fa rows live in
SEPARATE tables under separate headers — fa rows carry a ⭐ marker, the
"self-reported, not on the official leaderboard" label, and a footnote
with run date, fa version, dataset version, and the GitHub run link(s).
They are never sorted into or styled like official rows.

Official rows come from fetch.py (Harbor Hub API -> tbench.ai page-JSON
fallback). `--offline` reads the committed snapshots instead — the
snapshots keep README regeneration reproducible and let the auto-update
step degrade to the last captured board instead of failing when the hub
is unreachable. A version with no official rows and no snapshot renders
an explicit "no official rows" note — never an empty table that could
read as an empty field.

Regenerating with unchanged inputs leaves README.md untouched (the
workflow's commit step relies on that for idempotency).

Stdlib only.
"""
import argparse
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import fetch
import record

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPO_ROOT = HERE.parent.parent
README_PATH = REPO_ROOT / "README.md"
SNAPSHOT_DIR = HERE / "snapshots"

MARKER_BEGIN = "<!-- leaderboard:begin (gh-1682) -->"
MARKER_END = "<!-- leaderboard:end (gh-1682) -->"
INSERT_BEFORE_HEADING = "## What's inside"
# README section header lives inside the marked region, so removing the
# markers removes the whole section.
SECTION_HEADER = "## Leaderboard: fa vs. the field"
FA_MARKER = "⭐"

DEFAULT_OFFICIAL_VERSIONS = ("4.0",)


def pct(part: int, total: int) -> str:
    return f"{100.0 * part / total:.1f}%" if total else "n/a"


def _link(label: str, url: str) -> str:
    return f"[{label}]({url})" if url else label


def _run_link(url: str) -> str:
    """A GitHub Actions run URL renders by its run id (the stable,
    auditable handle) — full URLs in every cell would drown the table."""
    run_id = url.rstrip("/").rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    return _link(run_id, url)


def render_official_table(doc: dict, top: int) -> "list[str]":
    rows = doc.get("rows") or []
    shown = rows[:top]
    lines = [
        "| # | Agent | Model | Accuracy | Trials | Date |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for i, r in enumerate(shown, 1):
        lines.append(
            "| {rank} | {agent} | {model} | {acc} | {n} | {date} |".format(
                rank=r.get("rank") or i,
                agent=_link(r["agent"], r.get("agent_url")) or "—",
                model=_link(r["model"], r.get("model_url")) or "—",
                acc=pct_1(r.get("accuracy")),
                n=r.get("n_trials") or "—",
                date=r.get("date") or "—",
            )
        )
    fetched = (doc.get("fetched_at") or "")[:10]
    note = (
        f"Official rows: Harbor Hub leaderboard "
        f"`{doc.get('package')}/{doc.get('leaderboard')}` — "
        f"backing [tbench.ai](https://www.tbench.ai/)"
    )
    if len(rows) > len(shown):
        note += f", top {len(shown)} of {len(rows)}"
    if fetched:
        note += f", fetched {fetched}"
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"<sub>{note}.</sub>")
    return lines


def pct_1(accuracy) -> str:
    """Hub accuracy is a 0-100 percentage; render one decimal."""
    if accuracy is None:
        return "n/a"
    return f"{float(accuracy):.1f}%"


def render_fa_table(rows: "list[dict]", version: str) -> "list[str]":
    lines = [
        "| Model | Accuracy | Trials | Date | fa | Runs |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for r in rows:
        runs = " + ".join(_run_link(u) for u in r.get("run_urls") or []) or "—"
        fa = r.get("fa_version") or "—"
        lines.append(
            f"| {FA_MARKER} {r.get('model', '—')} "
            f"| {pct(r.get('resolved', 0), r.get('total', 0))} "
            f"| {r.get('resolved', '—')}/{r.get('total', '—')} "
            f"| {r.get('date', '—')} "
            f"| `{fa}` "
            f"| {runs} |"
        )
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(
        f"<sub>{FA_MARKER} Self-reported: measured by our own "
        f"`bench-harbor` runs on Terminal-Bench {version}, **not** an "
        "official leaderboard submission (community submissions are "
        "closed — #1681). Every row links its GitHub Actions run(s); fa "
        "rows never blend into the official table above. Source: "
        "`bench/leaderboard/fa_results.json`.</sub>"
    )
    return lines


def render_version_section(version: str, official: dict,
                           fa_rows: "list[dict]", top: int,
                           offline_note: bool) -> str:
    title = (official or {}).get("title") or f"Terminal-Bench {version}"
    lines = [f"### {title} (official)", ""]
    if official and official.get("rows"):
        lines += render_official_table(official, top)
    else:
        source = "committed snapshot" if offline_note else "live fetch"
        lines += [
            f"*No official leaderboard rows for Terminal-Bench {version} "
            f"right now ({source} returned none — the board may not exist "
            "yet or the hub may be unreachable). See the fa self-reported "
            "rows below and [tbench.ai](https://www.tbench.ai/).*",
        ]
    if fa_rows:
        lines += [
            "",
            f"#### fa on Terminal-Bench {version} — self-reported "
            f"{FA_MARKER} (not on the official leaderboard)",
            "",
        ] + render_fa_table(fa_rows, version)
    return "\n".join(lines)


def render_section(versions: "list[str]", official_by_version: "dict[str, dict]",
                   ledger: dict, top: int, offline_notes: "set[str]") -> str:
    fa_by_version = {}
    for row in ledger.get("results") or []:
        fa_by_version.setdefault(row.get("dataset_version"), []).append(row)
    for rows in fa_by_version.values():
        rows.sort(key=lambda r: -(r.get("resolved", 0) / r.get("total", 1) or 0))

    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).date().isoformat()
    parts = [
        SECTION_HEADER,
        "",
        "fa's own Terminal-Bench results next to the official field. "
        "Official rows are read from the Harbor Hub leaderboard that "
        "backs [tbench.ai](https://www.tbench.ai/); rows marked "
        f"{FA_MARKER} are **self-reported** — measured by our own "
        "bench-harbor runs, not submitted to the official board.",
        "",
        f"<sub>Regenerated {now} by "
        "`bench/leaderboard/render.py` (gh-1682).</sub>",
        "",
    ]
    for version in versions:
        parts.append(
            render_version_section(
                version, official_by_version.get(version),
                fa_by_version.get(version, []), top,
                version in offline_notes,
            )
        )
        parts.append("")
    return "\n".join(parts).rstrip() + "\n"


def splice_readme(text: str, section: str) -> str:
    """Replace the marked region (or insert before the anchor heading)."""
    begin = text.find(MARKER_BEGIN)
    end = text.find(MARKER_END)
    block = f"{MARKER_BEGIN}\n{section}{MARKER_END}\n"
    if begin >= 0 and end > begin:
        return text[:begin] + block + text[end + len(MARKER_END) + 1:]
    anchor = text.find(INSERT_BEFORE_HEADING)
    if anchor < 0:
        return text.rstrip() + "\n\n" + block

# Leaderboards

> Create, rank, and share evaluation results on Harbor Hub.

A leaderboard is a ranked table of results for a dataset. You define its columns and ranking rules, add rows with metadata and scores, and optionally link each row to the trials behind it.

<Note>
  Harbor Hub intentionally does not calculate row scores from linked trials, to enable maximally flexible leaderboard construction.
</Note>

blocks.text:
1. Choose a published dataset and the [versions](#dataset-versions) the leaderboard will cover.
2. [Generate a configuration](#create) with `init`, then define the metadata, metrics, columns, and ranking rules.
3. Prepare your results as [rows](#add-rows), calculating the scores yourself. Include trial IDs if you want to link each result to its runs.
4. Create the leaderboard with its definition and rows files. Keep it private while reviewing the results.
5. [Inspect the leaderboard](#browse), check the rankings and trial links, then [make it public](#edit-a-leaderboard) when it is ready.

## Browse

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor hub leaderboard list
harbor hub leaderboard list "<org>/<dataset>"
harbor hub leaderboard show "<leaderboard>"
```

`list` optionally filters by dataset slug or ID.

## Create

Generate a configuration file, edit it, then create the leaderboard:

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor auth login
harbor hub leaderboard init \
  --package "<org>/<dataset>" \
  --name main \
  --title "Main leaderboard" \
  --output leaderboard.yaml
# Edit leaderboard.yaml.
harbor hub leaderboard create --config leaderboard.yaml
```

New leaderboards are private. Set `visibility: public` in the file or pass `--visibility public` to `create`.

### Configuration schema

The definition file passed to `create --config` accepts the fields below. Use either `package` or `package_id`. Rows go in a separate file passed with `--rows`.

<ParamField body="package" type="string">
  Dataset slug, such as `acme/my-dataset`. Required unless `package_id` is provided.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="package_id" type="string (UUID)">
  Dataset package UUID, as an alternative to `package`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="name" type="string" required>
  Leaderboard slug, up to 100 characters. Starts with a lowercase letter or digit; may also contain `.`, `_`, and `-`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="title" type="string" required>
  Display title, from 1 to 200 characters.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="description" type="string | null">
  Optional description, up to 5,000 characters.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="visibility" type="string" default="private">
  `public` or `private`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="metadata_schema" type="object" default="{}">
  Schema for each row's metadata, such as the agent name and configuration.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="metrics_schema" type="object" default="{}">
  Schema for each row's metrics, such as scores and costs.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="columns" type="object[]" default="[]">
  Display columns, in left-to-right order.

  <Expandable title="Column fields">
    <ParamField body="id" type="string" required>
      Unique column key. Starts with a letter, digit, or underscore; may also contain `.` and `-`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="header" type="string" required>
      Non-empty display heading.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="accessor" type="string" required>
      Value path beginning with `metadata.` or `metrics.`, such as `metrics.reward`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="type" type="string" required>
      `text`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `markdown`, or `link`. Links accept a URL string or an object with `url` and `label`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="display_accessor" type="string">
      Alternate value path for display. The original `accessor` remains the sort value.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="display_type" type="string">
      Formatter for the alternate display value; accepts the same values as `type`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="align" type="string">
      `left`, `center`, or `right`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="description" type="string">
      Explanation of the column.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="enable_sorting" type="boolean">
      Whether users can sort by this column in Hub.
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="rank_by" type="object[]" default="[]">
  Ranking rules, evaluated in order to break ties.

  <Expandable title="Ranking rule fields">
    <ParamField body="accessor" type="string" required>
      Value path beginning with `metadata.` or `metrics.`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="direction" type="string" required>
      `asc` for lowest first or `desc` for highest first.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="nulls" type="string">
      Place missing values `first` or `last`.
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="dataset_version_refs" type="string[]">
  Dataset version refs to associate, such as `latest` or a version tag. Resolved to fixed UUIDs at creation.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="dataset_version_ids" type="string (UUID)[]">
  Dataset version UUIDs to associate. Can be combined with refs. Omit both fields to associate all existing versions; set both to `[]` for none.
</ParamField>

### Columns and ranking

The generated file includes an example with an agent name and reward score:

```yaml theme={"system"}
metadata_schema:
  type: object
  properties:
    agent:
      type: string
metrics_schema:
  type: object
  properties:
    reward:
      type: number
columns:
  - id: agent
    header: Agent
    accessor: metadata.agent
    type: text
  - id: reward
    header: Reward
    accessor: metrics.reward
    type: number
rank_by:
  - accessor: metrics.reward
    direction: desc
    nulls: last
```

This displays an agent column and a reward column, with the highest reward ranked first.

### Dataset versions

By default, a new leaderboard is associated with every dataset version that exists at creation time. Later versions are not added automatically.

To select versions explicitly, add `dataset_version_refs` or `dataset_version_ids` to the configuration:

```yaml theme={"system"}
dataset_version_refs:
  - latest
```

Refs resolve to fixed version UUIDs. Both fields can be combined; setting both to `[]` associates no versions.

## Add rows

Create `rows.yaml` with the values your columns expect:

```yaml theme={"system"}
rows:
  - metadata:
      agent: Example agent
    metrics:
      reward: 0.85
```

Then add the rows:

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor hub leaderboard row create "<leaderboard>" --config rows.yaml
```

### Row file schema

The file passed to `row create --config` or `create --rows` has this structure:

<ParamField body="rows" type="object[]" required>
  Between 1 and 500 new rows. Trial IDs must be unique across the rows in the request.

  <Expandable title="Row fields">
    <ParamField body="metadata" type="object" default="{}">
      Values matching the leaderboard's `metadata_schema`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="metrics" type="object" default="{}">
      Values matching the leaderboard's `metrics_schema`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="status" type="string" default="display">
      `display` to show the row or `hide` to hide it.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField body="trial_ids" type="string (UUID)[]" default="[]">
      Trials linked to this row. Linking trials does not compute metadata or metrics.
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

To create the leaderboard and its rows together, pass the separate rows file to `create`:

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor hub leaderboard create --config leaderboard.yaml --rows rows.yaml
```

## Edit a leaderboard

Change its title, description, or visibility directly:

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor hub leaderboard update "<leaderboard>" \
  --title "Updated leaderboard" --visibility public
```

Use `--description` to change the description or `--visibility private` to make the board private. To replace dataset-version associations, repeat `--dataset-version-ref` or `--dataset-version-id`. Omit these fields to preserve existing associations.

For columns, schemas, or ranking changes, export the definition, edit it, then apply it:

```bash theme={"system"}
harbor hub leaderboard export "<leaderboard>" --output leaderboard.yaml
# Edit leaderboard.yaml.
harbor hub leaderboard update "<leaderboard>" --config leaderboard.yaml
```

    # test harnesses load this module without the dir on sys.path.

            # families.py before dispatch, but a direct summary call must
            # not silently render a mis-keyed report.
            print(
                f"::error::unknown Terminal-Bench family '{args.family}' —"
                f" resolve the dataset id first (families.py resolve);"
                f" known: {', '.join(sorted(families.FAMILIES))}",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2

        title = f"### fa on Terminal-Bench {args.family} ({families.FAMILIES[args.family]})"
        ledger = {
            "dataset": families.FAMILIES[args.family],
            "model": args.model or "—",
            "fa_ref": args.fa_ref or "—",
            "run_url": args.run_url or "—",
        }

    lines, problems = render(
        splits,
        args.expected_trials,
        title=title,
        ledger=ledger,
        run_label=os.environ.get("BENCH_RUN_LABEL", "").strip() or None,
        expected_shards=args.expected_shards,

            f.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    else:
        print("\n".join(lines))

    return 0 if not problems else 1

# gh-1638 AC4 (the systemic lesson): the bench-script python tests ran
# ONLY inside the bench workflows' setup jobs (dispatch-gated), so the
# Oct-14 merge wave rotted them on main invisibly for 3+ days — every
# dispatch died at setup while the main quality gate (dart test / coverage
# / guards) never executes a line of python. This job runs the EXACT setup
# gate (same discovery roots, same pinned deps) on every bench/** change:
# a red bench-script test now fails the PR and main cannot rot silently.
name: Bench script tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Superseded PR runs die instantly; main-push runs are never cancelled
# mid-flight (same release-protection principle as ci.yml).
concurrency:
  group: Bench script tests-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
